One request, end to end

Follow one request through the stack

A customer disputes an invoice. Watch the request move from the channel to the system of record, and see which layer does what.

  1. Channels and signals. The dispute arrives by email.
  2. Human command. The charter and the do-not-automate list set the limits.
  3. Orchestration. The workflow engine starts the dispute flow.
  4. Agents. The finance agent investigates.
  5. Intelligence. A GPT-class model reads the contract; retrieval grounds it.
  6. Harness. Policy limits, the decision threshold and verification check the proposal.
  7. Tools and integration. A released interface commits the credit.
  8. Data and context. The system of record and the ledger tie out.
  9. Assurance. The trace, evals and audit keep the evidence.

Alignment across every layer

Alignment across every layer

Every agent action must agree across the financial, regulatory, operational, application and technical layers of the enterprise.

Pick a layer. Each item shows what the agent does, how the layer stays consistent with the others, the controls that enforce it and the evidence. The same layers filter the architecture, the workflows, the controls and the designer.

Financial

Agents prepare and propose money movements. The ledger, the limits and the trace must always agree.

  1. Credits and adjustments
    What the agent does
    The agent investigates a dispute and proposes a credit memo.
    Alignment check
    A posted credit ties to the general ledger, the policy limit and the audit trail.
    Controls embedded
    TAL-01 TAL-02 DQ-04 TRC-01
    Evidence
    Daily tie-out report. Trace ID on every posting.
  2. Invoice exceptions
    What the agent does
    The agent resolves price and quantity variances inside tolerance.
    Alignment check
    The purchase order, the receipt and the invoice agree before release.
    Controls embedded
    TAL-01 DQ-01 SOD-03
    Evidence
    Match results. Version of the tolerance table.
  3. Close and reconciliations
    What the agent does
    The agent prepares reconciliations and proposes journals.
    Alignment check
    Subledger equals ledger. The preparer is never the approver.
    Controls embedded
    DQ-04 SOD-01 HO-01
    Evidence
    Signed reconciliations. Journal approval log.
  4. Payments and bank data
    What the agent does
    The agent prepares evidence only. It never releases money or changes bank details.
    Alignment check
    No agent holds a payment-release or bank-change permission.
    Controls embedded
    TAL-05 TAL-07 IAM-03
    Evidence
    Permission report with zero agent payment scopes.
  5. Cost of agent work
    What the agent does
    The agent records its spend per case.
    Alignment check
    Cost per completed outcome matches the finance allocation.
    Controls embedded
    CST-01 CST-02
    Evidence
    Monthly cost report reconciled to platform invoices.

Regulatory and statutory

Laws and standards set hard edges. Every step shows which rule applies and who signs.

  1. Human oversight where law requires it
    What the agent does
    The agent routes reserved decisions to named people.
    Alignment check
    The level of a step never exceeds its legal ceiling.
    Controls embedded
    HO-01 HO-02 TAL-05 RES-01
    Evidence
    Oversight design record. Approver logs.
  2. Record-keeping
    What the agent does
    The agent writes a trace for every decision.
    Alignment check
    Retention meets the statute, and each trace links to the record it supports.
    Controls embedded
    TRC-01 TRC-02 PRV-03
    Evidence
    Retention schedule. Trace samples.
  3. Key financial controls
    What the agent does
    Agent steps inside key controls stay at L2 until audit approves more.
    Alignment check
    The control matrix, the agent registry and the release log name the same steps.
    Controls embedded
    SOD-01 SOD-02 TRC-04 MR-02
    Evidence
    Control matrix with agent steps flagged. Audit sign-off.
  4. Privacy
    What the agent does
    The agent uses the minimum personal data.
    Alignment check
    The lawful basis for each field matches the context allow-list.
    Controls embedded
    PRV-01 PRV-02 PRV-03
    Evidence
    Data protection assessment. Masking logs.
  5. Machine and product safety
    What the agent does
    Physical AI runs inside rated safety functions.
    Alignment check
    No AI output can override the safety controller.
    Controls embedded
    PHY-01 PHY-02 PHY-03 OT-03
    Evidence
    Safety validation report. Risk assessment.
  6. Transparency
    What the agent does
    The agent tells people that they deal with an agent.
    Alignment check
    Every channel plays the same approved notice.
    Controls embedded
    PRV-04 HO-03
    Evidence
    Notice scripts. Call samples.

Operational

Agents run the work. Service levels, capacity and exceptions must stay in line with the plan.

  1. Service levels
    What the agent does
    The agent works the queue and escalates hard cases.
    Alignment check
    Escalations meet the same service level as agent-closed cases.
    Controls embedded
    HO-03 MON-01
    Evidence
    Service-level report by path.
  2. Exception routing
    What the agent does
    The agent sends each exception to one owner.
    Alignment check
    Every exception has an owner and lands in one inbox.
    Controls embedded
    HO-01 TAL-02
    Evidence
    Queue aging report.
  3. Capacity and envelope
    What the agent does
    The agent runs inside call, time and cost budgets.
    Alignment check
    Run budgets match planned volumes.
    Controls embedded
    CST-01 RES-03 TAL-04
    Evidence

  4. Field and plant work
    What the agent does
    The agent drafts work orders from sensor signals.
    Alignment check

    Controls embedded
    DQ-03 OT-04 HO-01
    Evidence
    Work order audit sample.
  5. Continuity
    What the agent does
    On an outage, work falls back to people without loss.
    Alignment check

    Controls embedded
    RES-02 RES-01 RES-04
    Evidence
    Drill records.

Application

Agents act through applications. Every action uses a released interface and the rules of that application.

  1. Released interfaces only
    What the agent does
    The agent calls tools, not screens.
    Alignment check
    Each tool maps to a versioned interface with the validations of the application.
    Controls embedded
    TAL-03 IAM-03
    Evidence
    Tool registry matched to the interface catalogue.
  2. Business rules stay in the application
    What the agent does
    The agent proposes a change.
    Alignment check
    The application validates the proposal again before commit.
    Controls embedded
    PCS-02 TAL-02
    Evidence
    Rejection logs.
  3. Idempotency and reversal
    What the agent does
    The agent commits through one key per action.
    Alignment check
    Each action can be reversed once, and only once.
    Controls embedded
    TAL-06
    Evidence
    Reversal tests.
  4. Registry and versions
    What the agent does
    Only registered agent versions run.
    Alignment check
    The registry, the release log and the running version agree.
    Controls embedded
    MR-03 SOD-02 TRC-04
    Evidence
    Release records.
  5. Cross-agent contracts
    What the agent does
    Agents hand work to other agents.
    Alignment check
    Each contract names who decides, what evidence returns and the failure path.
    Controls embedded
    TAL-03 HO-02
    Evidence
    Contract library.

  1. Policy engine

    What the agent does

  3. Identity and tokens

  4. Resilience

Built on the book

Every blueprint traces to a framework

FrameworkWhere it shows in the blueprints
L0 to L5 scaleEvery component, step and control carries a level.
Materiality and reversibilityThe designer computes each ceiling with the five modifiers.
Ten-part harnessThe control plane layer of the architecture, and the heatmap on the controls page.
Propose, validate, route, commitThe harness lane of every reimagined workflow.
Decision thresholdThe designer computes L ÷ (G + L) per step.
Weakest-link ruleEach workflow shows its chain level and the link that holds it.
Cost per completed outcomeBefore and after cards on each workflow.
Do-not-automate listControl TAL-05, and the supplier bank change that stays with people.
Value-risk flywheelDrift, demotion and override labels in the assurance layer.

All figures in the blueprints are illustrative. They are not client data.
